summary: Detect a call cycle on a tiny graph
description: Return True when A calls B and B calls A. Return False for a two-node chain with no back edge.
scope: Cyclic fixture: A -> B and B -> A returns True
Acyclic fixture: A -> B returns False
acceptanceCriteria: has_cycle returns True for A->B plus B->A, and False for A->B only.
constraints: Strict TDD: write the failing test first and run it before implementation.
Do not add UI, watcher, or CLI code unless this task explicitly requires it.
Do not scan the fixtures folder.

subtasks.title: True on a two-node cycle, False on a chain
subtasks.summary: One boolean function. Two tiny in-memory graphs. No serialization.
scope: Cyclic fixture: A -> B and B -> A returns True
Acyclic fixture: A -> B returns False
dataExamples: Cyclic edges: A -> B, B -> A.
businessRules: A cycle exists when a directed path returns to its start.
Self-loops count as cycles if they appear, but the required fixtures are A<->B and A->B.
instructions: Write the failing test in tests/test_cycles.py first.
Run python -m pytest tests/test_cycles.py -q and confirm failure.
Run python -m pytest tests/test_cycles.py -q and stop when it passes.
